sections.content: How many people stayed in Kingston upon Hull after gaining qualifications?

Kingston upon Hull is a city in Yorkshire and The Humber. Kingston upon Hull also has a university.

Kingston upon Hull has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Kingston upon Hull ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 13,710 state-school pupils from Kingston upon Hull who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 3,035 (22%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 4,125 (30%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Kingston upon Hull to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Kingston upon Hull's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Kingston upon Hull in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Kingston upon Hull move to?

Of Kingston upon Hull's graduates, 845 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 150 of those graduates (18%) were living fairly locally, in the Hull travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Kingston upon Hull's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 480 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 200 of those qualified non-graduates (42%) were living fairly locally, in the Hull travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Kingston upon Hull's GCSE cohort:

  • 480 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 195 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 33% of graduates and 17% of qualified non-graduates living in Kingston upon Hull had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 3,220 graduates and 4,315 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Kingston upon Hull. This is compared with the 3,035 graduates and 4,125 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 67% of the graduates had also lived in Kingston upon Hull as GCSE pupils, while 33% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Kingston upon Hull in 2018 to 2019, 83% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 17% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
